package modal

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/core"
	modal "github.com/modal-labs/modal-client/go"
)

type Config struct {
	TokenID    string
	TokenSecret string
}

type Adapter struct {
	client *modal.Client
}

func New(cfg Config) (*Adapter, error) {
	client, err := modal.NewClient(
		// Illustrative: use the actual Modal SDK constructor/config.
		modal.WithToken(cfg.TokenID, cfg.TokenSecret),
	)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return &Adapter{client: client}, nil
}

func (a *Adapter) CreateSandbox(
	ctx context.Context,
	opts core.SandboxOptions,
) (any, error) {
	app, err := a.client.Apps.FromName(ctx, opts.Name, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	image := a.client.Images.FromRegistry(opts.Image, nil)

	return a.client.Sandboxes.Create(ctx, app, image, &modal.SandboxCreateParams{
		// Map only fields Modal supports.
		Region: opts.Region,
	})
}

func (a *Adapter) GetSandbox(
	ctx context.Context,
	id string,
) (any, error) {
	return a.client.Sandboxes.FromID(ctx, id, nil)
}

func (a *Adapter) DeleteSandbox(
	ctx context.Context,
	id string,
) error {
	sandbox, err := a.client.Sandboxes.FromID(ctx, id, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	_, err = sandbox.Terminate(ctx, nil)

}

# config

Modal client configuration.

Configuration values are read from the active profile in `.modal.toml`. Each setting can be overridden by an environment variable named `MODAL_<SETTING>`.

Client processes can authenticate in two ways:

  1. Modal API tokens use `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET`. The `modal token set` command stores these values in `.modal.toml`.
  2. Third-party OAuth integrations typically inject `MODAL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `MODAL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, and `MODAL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` into the process.

The two authentication methods cannot be combined, and all values for the selected method must be provided.

## .modal.toml

The `.modal.toml` file is generally stored in your home directory. It should look like this::
    
    `[default]
    token_id = "ak-12345..."
    token_secret = "as-12345..."`

You can create this file manually, or you can run the `modal token set ...` command (see below).

## Setting tokens using the CLI

You can set a token by running the command::
    
    `modal token set \
      --token-id <token id> \
      --token-secret <token secret>`

This will write the token id and secret to `.modal.toml`.

If the token id or secret is provided as the string `-` (a single dash), then it will be read in a secret way from stdin instead.
